To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a boil water notice is not an effective means to control the risks of waterborne infection; 2) the majority of people do not boil their water, and many do not change their behaviour at all when a boil water notice has been issued; 3) the notice was not well received by the public; and 4) the notice is not an appropriate way to communicate with the public about a water contamination incident.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect on behaviour of the public health measures used to manage a water contamination incident and with the effectiveness of these measures in reducing the risk of water-borne infection.
understanding the relationship between the public health response to a water contamination incident and consumer behaviour in relation to water consumption.
the impact of a boil water advisory on the behaviours and attitudes of consumers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the notice was not followed by a significant change in risk behaviour.
the notice had a negligible effect on behaviour in this community.
a boil water notice is ineffective in modifying behaviour that might lead to waterborne infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a boil water notice is an ineffective means of controlling waterborne infection in an incident involving possible sewage contamination.
there is no doubt that the boil water notice was effective in reducing waterborne infection risk behaviour.

there is an urgent need to improve the way in which water authorities and health authorities communicate with the public in the event of a water contamination episode, and to improve the way that the public responds to such an event.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a boil water notice is unlikely to be effective in reducing the risk of water-borne infections.
a significant proportion of the population is likely to engage in risky behaviour during a boil water notice, even if they are aware of the risk of infection.
a boil water notice did not lead to a reduction in the number of people who continued to engage in activities that might increase the risk of infection.
